result:
Admins can now change a user's role from the users list. Each row except your own shows a role select. Changing it sends `PATCH /users/{userId}/role` with `{ role }`, shows a "User Role Updated" notification, and refreshes the list. I did not run tests, lint, or the app, as you asked.

What changed in `apps/react-vite`:

- **API:** `src/features/users/api/update-user-role.ts` has the Zod schema, the `updateUserRole` fetcher, and `useUpdateUserRole`. The hook invalidates the users query and shows the success notification, following the features rule.
- **Component:** `src/features/users/components/update-user-role.tsx` renders a `Select` from `@/components/ui/form`. It fires the mutation on change. If the server rejects the change, the select reverts to the previous role.
- **List:** `users-list.tsx` uses the new component in the Role column.
- **Policy:** `src/lib/authorization.tsx` gets a `user:update-role` policy: admin only, and not on your own row. Your own row shows the role as plain text, so an admin can't demote themselves from the list.
- **Mock API:** `src/testing/mocks/handlers/users.ts` adds an MSW handler for the PATCH endpoint, so the feature works in dev without a backend. It returns 401, 400, 404 or 500 where appropriate.

Lint hook findings: the hook flagged the string literals `'ADMIN'` and `'USER'` in the two feature files (`local/roles-from-enum`). I changed them to `ROLES.ADMIN` and `ROLES.USER`, and the schema now uses `z.nativeEnum(ROLES)`. I did not change the rule or add ignore comments. I also used `ROLES` in the new policy line. The hook has not re-run since those edits, so the fixes are unverified.

Things to check:

- The repo has no real backend, so the endpoint exists only in the MSW mock. A real server must implement `PATCH /users/:userId/role` with the same contract.
- The existing `DeleteUser` component still compares ids directly (`user.data?.id === id`). I left it alone because it is outside this change.
